Alright, I've been iteratively tweaking the water simulation shader to improve visual quality: adjusting color grading, foam intensity, mist, foam decay, splash radius, normal strength, reflection blend, and overall water color. After each set of changes I generated screenshots at two key times (mid‑collapse around ff=1.2 s and a later settling point at ff=8 s) to see how the adjustments look. The screenshots (shot2‑shot5) didn't show any obvious issues, but I still suspect the dynamics could be further refined, especially around the peak of the splash and the later calm phase.

Looking at the timeline of the simulation, the most visually interesting moments are roughly at 2.5 s (when the splash is fully developed) and around 12 s (when the water has largely settled but still shows subtle ripples and reflections). I haven't captured those points yet, so I need new screenshots at those timestamps to evaluate the cumulative effect of all the recent edits.

Given the pattern I've used so far, the appropriate way to capture screenshots is via a headless Chrome PowerShell command. The command format is:

```
& "C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe" --headless=new --use-angle=swiftshader --window-size=1280,720 --virtual-time-budget=1500 --screenshot="PATH\shotX.png" "file:///D:/physics/New folder/water-simulation.html?ff=TIME" 2>&1 | Out-Null;
```

I need two screenshots: one at ff=2.5 and another at ff=12. Following the naming convention, these will be `shot6.png` and `shot7.png`. I'll place them in the same folder as the previous shots (`D:\physics\New folder`). After both commands, I should output `"done"` to signal completion, and include a description for clarity.

The timeout of 240 000 ms (4 minutes) has been sufficient for earlier captures, so I'll keep that. This will give me the final visual reference to confirm whether the recent parameter tweaks have achieved the desired look across the full simulation timeline.

Thus, the next step is to invoke the PowerShell tool with the constructed command, targeting the two new timestamps and saving the results as `shot6.png` and `shot7.png`. This aligns with the established workflow and will provide the necessary data for the next evaluation phase.
